name: Kettuvallam — the Rice Barge
tagline: The plank-and-coir cargo boat that became the backwater houseboat
summary: Kettuvallam, Kerala's traditional rice barge: how it is built without nails, its history in the spice and rice trade, and how to choose an authentic boat.
description: A kettuvallam is a traditional backwater boat made of jackwood planks tied with coir rope and sealed with cashew-nut oil and resin, with a curved roof of woven palm leaves. The name means 'boat of knots'.
Once used to carry rice and spices across Kuttanad and Vembanad, many were converted into the houseboats that now carry tourists.

history.significance: A masterpiece of vernacular boatbuilding that tells the story of Kerala's inland trade.

timeline.event: Plank-built, coir-sewn boats carry rice and spices along the backwaters to ports such as Alappuzha and Kollam.
Roads and trucks replace the cargo boats; many are abandoned or sold.
Converted kettuvallams are re-fitted as houseboats, launching backwater tourism.

keyFacts: Planks are stitched with coir and sealed without nails.
Roofs are woven from palm fronds.
Traditional boats are made of anjili (jackwood) or similar timber.
Registered houseboats are subject to rules on waste and safety.

folklore.title: The Boat of Knots
story: Boatbuilders say the tying of the knots is a skill passed from father to son, and each family has its own way of binding the planks. A new boat is launched with a small ritual and a coconut offered to the water.
Boat-songs (vanchippattu) are sung by crews to keep rhythm, and the oldest verses are said to recall the journeys of grain boats.

spiritual.summary: A slow day on a kettuvallam is a lesson in how Kerala's water roads once worked.

experiences.title: Choose an eco-friendly boat
experiences.text: Book a registered boat with waste-handling and low-noise engines.

experiences.title: Visit a boatyard
experiences.text: Ask your host to arrange a visit to a boatyard to see coir-stitching and caulking.

mindfulTips: Keep noise low near villages and bird areas.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November to February; boat-race season is August–September.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Houseboats start from Alappuzha, Kumarakom and Kollam jetties.

heritage.materials: Jackwood planks, coir rope, cashew-nut oil, palm leaves

whereToBuy.name: Registered houseboat operators (DTPC-approved)
whereToBuy.note: Use boats registered with the District Tourism Promotion Council; ask for the registration certificate.

experiences.name: Kuttanad village and rice-farm walks
experiences.note: Community-run experiences available through homestays (verify operators).

buyingTips: Prefer boats with a green or eco rating and a visible licence.
Avoid bargain boats with unclear safety kit.
